answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a nectar as the anchor of the cost.
